# Results — Study 869 (52-Week-High Breakout Drift)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — when a
stock closes at a **fresh 52-week high** (a breakout *event*, not George-Hwang *nearness* —
that is study 236), does it **drift up** (breakout momentum) or **fade** (resistance)? We flag
each name's new-52-week-high days point-in-time and measure the forward 5/20-day return of a
long-just-broke-out book vs the rest. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete
calendar month; the partial current month is dropped — the run is stamped as-of 2026-06-30).
Fingerprint `357fd262912f` (panel Close).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLC (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return), **50 liquid US large-caps**, 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30, **4,147** dated rows/name |
| Universe | a fixed `UNIVERSE` of ~50 mega-caps, pulled through the **`quantlab.universe` survivorship guard** (`download_panel(..., allow_survivorship_bias=True)`), cached under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Signal | a point-in-time **fresh 52-week-high breakout flag**: `Close[t]` strictly tops the rolling 252-day maximum of *prior* closes (`.rolling(252).max().shift(1)` — today excluded), known at the close of `t` |
| Sort | each day the **breakout book** = mean forward-`h` return of names that just broke out; the **rest book** = the names that did not; `spread = breakout − rest` (long just-broke-out, short the rest), `h ∈ {5, 20}` trading days |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: breakout at close `t` → **enter at close `t+1`**, hold `h` days (`fwd[t]=Close[t+1+h]/Close[t+1]−1`). The costed timer charges 2 sides × (in+out) one-way per event; the short book pays 50 bps/yr borrow |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC) *t* on the daily spread (lags = 2×horizon: the forward windows overlap); one-sample *t*; Welch *t* on the pooled breakout-vs-rest events; a 1,000-permutation placebo; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** `UNIVERSE` is a **current-membership** list of
names that are liquid mega-caps *today*, so the magnitudes are an **upper bound**. Crucially,
survivors *trend up*, which makes fresh 52-week highs both **more frequent** (14.6k breakout
observations here) and more likely to be followed by more up-days than in an unbiased tape — so
this panel is exactly where a breakout-drift, if anywhere, should look *strongest*.

## The headline — long-breakout / short-rest forward-return spread

Daily equal-weight breakout-minus-rest forward return, both horizons:

| horizon | event-days | spread | NW(2h) *t* | one-sample *t* | breakout book / rest book | Welch *t* | hit rate (Wilson95) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **5-day** | 3,039 | **+7.21 bps** | **+1.14** | +1.70 | +31.14 / +23.93 bps | +1.22 | 0.515 [0.497, 0.532] |
| **20-day** | 3,025 | **+21.64 bps** | **+1.20** | +2.48 | +131.09 / +109.45 bps | +1.75 | 0.506 [0.489, 0.524] |

The drift is in the **claimed direction** — a fresh 52-week-high name *out-earns* the rest over
the next week and month (breakout **momentum**, not the fade/resistance alternative). But the
magnitude does **not clear the significance bar**: the honest, overlap-corrected Newey-West *t*
is only **+1.14** (5-day) and **+1.20** (20-day). The 20-day one-sample *t* of +2.48 looks
tempting, but the forward windows overlap heavily, and once the HAC correction removes that
serial correlation the *t* collapses to +1.20. Indistinguishable from zero.

## Placebo — is the (small) drift a lucky alignment of the breakout flags?

Keep the breakout event flags but read each day's forward returns from a **column-permuted**
panel (event → outcome link broken), 1,000 permutations (20 seeds × 50):

| horizon | observed | placebo mean (sd) | right-tail p |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day | +7.21 bps | −0.044 bps (5.660) | **0.099** |
| 20-day | +21.64 bps | −0.284 bps (15.522) | **0.083** |

The permutation null centres at zero, and the observed spread sits ~1.3σ into the right tail —
**p ≈ 0.08–0.10**, above the 0.05 line. The drift is not a lucky flag alignment, but neither is
it distinguishable from noise.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2018-01-01)

| era | 5-day spread | NW *t* | 20-day spread | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2010-01 → 2018-01 | −1.50 bps | −0.24 | +10.34 bps | +0.57 |
| 2018-01 → 2026-06 | +14.72 bps | +1.40 | +31.47 bps | +1.06 |

The whole (weak) drift is a **2018-2026 phenomenon**: in 2010-2017 the 5-day spread is actually
slightly *negative* (breakouts faded), and neither era clears |*t*| = 2. It does **not hold
across sub-eras** — a red flag for any positive stamp.

## The timer — can you get paid for it?

Charge 2 sides × (in+out) one-way per event on the long-short book; short pays 50 bps/yr borrow.

| horizon | one-way | gross | cost | net | *t* (net) | Sharpe | ~ann. |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day | **1 bp** | +7.21 bps | 4.68 bps | **+2.52 bps** | +0.60 | 0.08 | +1.3%/yr |
| 5-day | **5 bps** | +7.21 bps | 20.68 bps | **−13.48 bps** | −3.18 | −0.41 | −6.8%/yr |
| 20-day | **1 bp** | +21.64 bps | 6.74 bps | **+14.90 bps** | +1.71 | 0.11 | +1.9%/yr |
| 20-day | **5 bps** | +21.64 bps | 22.74 bps | **−1.10 bps** | −0.13 | −0.01 | −0.1%/yr |

At an optimistic **1 bp** one-way the net edge is positive but **statistically insignificant**
(*t* = 0.60 / 1.71, annualised Sharpe ≈ 0.1); at a realistic **5 bps** it turns **negative**.
There is no cost that leaves a significant paycheck — a **Mirage**.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded panel: whenever a name printed a fresh 52-week high *yesterday*, `edge>0`
adds a small extra drift to the next 20 days (a planted breakout-momentum world). No network.

| world | spread NW *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.07** (sd 1.46), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** |
| planted (`edge = 0.0015`, seed 869) | **+9.62** (Welch *t* = +14.78) |

The detector recovers a *planted* breakout-drift cleanly and stays centred at zero on the null
(the lone fat-tailed seed reflects the clustered, sparse event structure, not bias) — so the
weak real-tape drift is a genuine feature of this tape, not an engine artefact.
*(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** A fresh 52-week-high breakout is followed by a **drift up**, not a fade —
  the sign matches the breakout-momentum reading (+7.21 bps over 5 days, +21.64 bps over 20 days,
  breakout book beats the rest on both). But the honest, overlap-corrected **Newey-West *t* is
  only +1.14 / +1.20**, the placebo p is **0.08–0.10**, and the effect is **entirely a 2018-2026
  phenomenon** (2010-2017 is flat-to-negative) — it fails the |*t*| ≥ 2 bar and does not hold
  across eras. Directionally there, statistically absent. *Survivorship: current-membership
  mega-caps — magnitudes are an upper bound (survivors over-print new highs).*
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Even at an optimistic 1 bp one-way the net edge is insignificant
  (*t* = 0.60 / 1.71, Sharpe ≈ 0.1) and it goes **negative** at a realistic 5 bps. No cost
  leaves a paycheck.
